text:
Predicates:
DeadlyDisease(x) ::: x is a deadly disease.
LowSurvivalRate(x) ::: x comes with a low survival rate.
SevereCancer(x) ::: x is a severe cancer.
BileDuctCancer(x) ::: x is bile duct cancer.
Cholangiocarcinoma(x) ::: x is Cholangiocarcinoma.
MildFlu(x) ::: x is mild flu.
ColorectalCancer(x) ::: x is colorectal cancer.
Form(x, y) ::: x is a form of y.
ComeWithLowSurvivalRate(x) ::: x comes with a low survival rate.
NotBoth(x, y, z) ::: x is not both y and z.
Premises:
∀x (DeadlyDisease(x) → LowSurvivalRate(x)) ::: If something is a deadly disease, then it comes with a low survival rate.
SevereCancer(cancer) ::: Severe cancers are deadly diseases.
Form(bileDuctCancer, cancer) ::: Bile duct cancer is a form of cancer.
All(Cholangiocarcinoma, bileDuctCancer) ::: All Cholangiocarcinoma is bile duct cancer.
MildFlu(x) → ComeWithLowSurvivalRate(x) ::: Mild flu comes with a low survival rate.
¬(Form(colorectalCancer, bileDuctCancer) ∧ ComeWithLowSurvivalRate(colorectalCancer)) ::: Colorectal cancer is not both a bile duct cancer and with a low survival rate.
Conclusion:
¬(Form(colorectalCancer, severeCancer)) ::: Colorectal cancer is not a kind of severe cancer.
